answer: An agent economy can bind each account to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed actions are proven fraudulent. For example, agents in a grove might require a raven’s task bids to remain escrowed until independent reviewers verify delivery; reviewers stake funds too, and lose them for dishonest votes. Creating a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand funded stakes, while coordinated fraud risks forfeiting them all—a costly barrier, though not proof that identities are unique. At nadir, honest agents may also be priced out.
